# Stress tests: bounds on the principle {#sec-stress}

When every layer can read every earlier position, relay is never necessary, and visible
content can always be re-read. We therefore test three settings that make relay useful
where attention cannot do the work, or make the content invisible, each with a decision
rule committed before its first result (@fig-stress; Appendix @sec-app-prereg,
@sec-app-stress and @sec-app-hidden).

![Stress tests. **A:** Qwen3.5 hybrids (three of every four layers recurrent), with the

attention layers (blue) accounts for nearly all of persistence; entry through the
recurrent layers (purple) produces 2 to 4%, below the committed stop line (10%); the
both-blocked cell is zero. **B:** Gemma 3 27B with filler between line 1 and line 2
(couplets per distance in brackets; the dotted line marks where line 1 leaves the
1,024-token window). Direct retrieval falls and the stored copy becomes necessary for
about half of persistence. The generated text (the cue and line 2, not split into late
lookup and relay) is 9 to 13%, between the committed stop and go lines. Side panels:
absolute persistence, and for four unedited models the share of couplets whose line 2

## Recurrent memory {#sec-recurrent}

Qwen3.5 [@qwen2026qwen35] interleaves three Gated DeltaNet layers
[@yang2025gateddeltanet] with each attention layer. In a recurrent layer, information
from the source can reach a later position only through a fixed-size state updated
position by position, invisible in the text; the attention layers can still look it up.
The test asks which path the model uses when both are available. In the *attention-only*
cell, the donor state enters at the source but the input of every recurrent layer there
is restored to its clean value; the *recurrent-only* cell is the converse. The committed
rule, decided on the largest model, was "go" if recurrent-only is at least 25% of
persistence and "stop" below 10%. Recurrent-only is 3% and 4% of persistence at 4B and
9B, and 2% at 27B (\(+0.41\) [0.18, 0.64] of \(+18.8\)); attention-only is 95 to 97%, and
blocking both cancels the donor on every couplet. Decision: stop. The design controls
which layer type receives the donor at the source, not every later path through each
type, so it bounds donor entry through recurrent memory at 2 to 4% of persistence.

## Beyond the attention window {#sec-distance}

Gemma 3 alternates five local layers with a 1,024-token window with one global layer
[@gemma3; @beltagy2020longformer], so once line 1 lies more than 1,024 tokens before the
target, five of six layers cannot read it. We insert up to 2,000 tokens of neutral
filler before line 2 and split the indirect path into the stored copy, the filler and the
generated text (the cue and line 2). The committed decision number was the share of
persistence through the generated text: "go" at 25%, "stop" below 10%, and an extension
to 50 couplets in between; a rise counts only if the absolute indirect effect also
grows. At 2,000 tokens Gemma 3 27B still rhymes in 82% of couplets. Direct retrieval
falls from 66% to 40% of persistence, and the stored copy at the line's final token
becomes necessary for about half (\(+13.0\) [10.0, 16.1] of \(+26.4\)); the filler passes
on nothing. The generated text accounts for 9 to 13% by sufficiency at every nonzero
distance (12% at 2,000 tokens, \(+3.2\) [2.2, 4.3]). It appears once filler is present
and does not grow further. It includes the last three positions, so it mixes relay with
the late lookup, and it falls between "stop" and "go": how much of it is relay remains
unresolved. The committed window prediction is only partly supported: the largest step is where line
1 leaves the window, but the shift begins at 500 tokens. Models without a strong stored
copy (Gemma 3 12B, and Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3-14B, whose attention has no window) lose the
plan instead, and in none of them does an indirect path take over. 

## Hidden content {#sec-hidden}

A choice that no reader can infer from the text is the case monitoring cares about
most. The prompt reads: "Secretly choose one fruit from this list: {4 fruits}. Do not
write your choice yet. First write one sentence about the weather. Then write the fruit
you chose." The greedy pick depends on the model's preferences and the list order, so no reader can
compute it. The donor is the list in another order with a different pick; the reference
is a *text swap* that writes that order into the prompt. In Qwen3-8B and Gemma 3 12B and 27B, donor states at the positions after the list
move the reveal by 12 to 16% of the text swap, all of it read directly; the part that
passes through the sentence is zero within its interval, and the rest of the pick is
presumably re-derived at the reveal from the visible list. In Qwen3-32B and the Qwen3.5
hybrids the indirect path through the sentence is small but nonzero: at most 2% of the
text swap, but one eighth to one fifth of the stored part. A sentence the model writes itself never names an item and has no measurable effect on
the reveal (emission \(-0.01\) to \(+0.02\)).

**The stored signal is pick-specific and sits at predictable tokens.** In an out-of-list
control, the donor's pick does not occur in the prompt at all, yet post-list donor states
raise it more than the donor's other items. This *pick specificity*, added post hoc for
fruits, was then committed as the primary measure of a replication with animals, which
confirms it in both families; a donor with the same pick leaves the preference unchanged.
The stored share is larger in Gemma and grows with generation (Gemma 3 15 to 40%, Gemma 4
31B 82 to 91% of the text swap's pick specificity), and it shrinks with scale in Qwen3 (0
to 7% at 14B and 32B). Per-token necessity places it on two or three low-content tokens: the periods that
close the list or the instruction, and one function word or possessive token of the
instruction (in Gemma 3 27B, 77% on *the* in "about the weather"). When the instruction
is reworded, the site moves with the wording at 4B, 12B and 27B (Appendix @fig-sites).
These controls do not distinguish a stored pick from a stored copy of the list, so we
claim only that pick-specific information absent from the text is stored after the list
and read at the reveal. As for rhymes, the copy is stored once, at a segment-closing or
predictable token, and read at the point of use.
